title: Planner: sprints and backlogs in unified plans
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing qualifications and administrative controls are supported. It correctly distinguishes current premium-plan entitlements from the still-undocumented rollout, storage and entitlement details for sprints in unified plans.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Premium plans are backed by Dataverse and their data is stored there.

claims.where: What's changing: Planner for admins
claims.claim: Microsoft's Planner for admins page says basic plans are now unified plans.
claims.quote: Basic plans are now unified plans.

claims.where: What's changing: Planner for admins
claims.claim: Premium capabilities are increasingly available in unified plans based on individual users' assigned licences.
claims.quote: Premium capabilities are increasingly available in unified plans based on the licenses assigned to individual users.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Members of a unified plan do not have to hold the same licence.
claims.quote: A unified plan doesn't require every member of the plan to have the same license.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Additional capabilities available to each unified-plan member depend on that member's Microsoft Copilot, Planner Plan 1 or Planner and Project Plan 3 licence.
claims.quote: Additional capabilities in unified plans are available based on whether the user has Microsoft Copilot, Planner Plan 1 or Planner and Project Plan 3.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether unified-plan sprints appear automatically or require an enabling action, so the default state is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner unified plans sprints backlogs automatically enabled default administrator switch Set-PlannerConfiguration. Read roadmap, Planner for admins, service description and returned Planner configuration excerpts; none states this feature's arrival default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model
claims.claim: Planner Plan 1 and Planner and Project Plan 3 use per-user subscription licensing.
claims.quote: Planner and Project Plan 3: $30.00 user/month, paid yearly; Planner Plan 1: $10.00 user/month, paid yearly.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Whether sprints in unified plans retain the existing premium-plan sprint entitlement is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner sprints backlogs unified plans licence Microsoft 365 view edit entitlement. Read service description, Planner for admins, trials and Planner pricing; sprints remain qualified as premium-plan-only, without a unified-plan sprint entitlement.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Users following prompts inside Planner can enable a 30-day Planner and Project Plan 3 trial.
claims.quote: When users follow the prompts in planner to enable a 30-day trial, they gain access to all the features and functionality available with a subscription license for Planner and Project Plan 3.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Trials
claims.claim: The Planner and Project Plan 3 trial includes sprints.
claims.quote: Plan 3 includes features such as task history, advanced dependencies, custom calendars, timeline (Gantt) view, sprints, custom fields, people view, and managing goals.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Trials; Governance guidance: licence request route
claims.claim: Users can request a Planner and Project Plan 3 licence from their administrator at the end of the trial.
claims.quote: At the end of the 30-day trial, they can request a Planner and Project Plan 3 license from their Microsoft 365 administrator.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Trials
claims.claim: Trial licences are also available for Planner Plan 1.
claims.quote: Trial licenses are also available for Planner Plan 1.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Trials
claims.claim: The MSCommerce reference lists Planner Plan 1 as having a trial without a payment method.
claims.quote: | Product | ProductId | Is trial without payment method enabled? | ... | Planner Plan 1* | CFQ7TTC0HDB1 | Yes |

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Plan access is defined by its container, which can be a group, meeting or channel.
claims.quote: Within Planner, each Plan is inside a container, and access to the plan is defined by the container. ... Plans can be inside other types of containers, like a Meeting or a Channel, and will use the membership defined by those containers.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Microsoft documents basic plan task data as stored in Azure.
claims.quote: The data of a basic plan, such as the titles and descriptions of tasks, are stored in Azure, encrypted at rest and in transit.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Microsoft's Planner Purview page lists premium plans as unsupported for eDiscovery.
claims.quote: eDiscovery content search and legal hold. ... Unsupported: Personal (roster) plans, plans in Loop components, premium plans (formerly projects), Shared and Private channel Plans (LWG backed Plans).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Roles
claims.claim: Microsoft states that there are no special administrative roles for Planner.
claims.quote: There are no special administrative roles for Planner. To take administrative action on a plan, use controls in Microsoft Entra to join the container (such as by adding yourself to a group).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The storage location of sprint and backlog data specifically in unified plans is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner unified plans sprint backlog data storage Azure Dataverse eDiscovery migration. Read Planner security, Purview, admins, service description and FAQ excerpts; they give plan/task storage but no storage mechanism for the new unified-plan sprint/backlog data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: What Microsoft 365-only members can see or edit in unified-plan sprints is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner sprints backlogs unified plans licence Microsoft 365 view edit entitlement. Read Planner service description and admins page; current premium-plan viewing rights are stated, but unified-plan sprint viewing/editing rights are not.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: row 1
claims.claim: User licence assignment is reached in Microsoft 365 admin center through Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. ... Select the row of the user ... select Licenses and Apps. ... Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: row 1
claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the specified user a licence using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: row 2
claims.claim: Blocking a product's self-service purchases and trials is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Services > Self-service trials and purchases > product > Do not allow.
claims.quote: Settings > Org settings ... On the Services tab ... select Self-service trials and purchases. ... select the product name. ... select Allow, Allow for trials only, or Do not allow.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: row 2
claims.claim: Update-MSCommerceProductPolicy -PolicyId AllowSelfServicePurchase -ProductId CFQ7TTC0HDB1 -Value "Disabled" disables Planner Plan 1 self-service purchases and trials.
claims.quote: Planner Plan 1* | CFQ7TTC0HDB1 | Yes; Disabled | Users can't make self-service purchases or acquire trials for the product.; Update-MSCommerceProductPolicy -PolicyId AllowSelfServicePurchase -ProductId <ProductID> -Value "Disabled"

claims.where: controls[1].note; Scope: Roles; Governance controls
claims.claim: Changing self-service trial and purchase settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center requires Global Administrator.
claims.quote: Use the Microsoft 365 admin center to allow or block self-service purchases and trials ... You must be a Global Administrator to do the following steps.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Scope: Roles; Governance controls
claims.claim: Changing MSCommerce product policies for the tenant requires Global or Billing Administrator.
claims.quote: The Global or Billing Administrator role for your tenant to change the MSCommerce product policies.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The self-service policy controls purchases and trials per product, including Planner Plan 1 and Project Plan 3, and each product must be set individually.
claims.quote: The AllowSelfServicePurchase policy is managed on a per-product basis. ... turning off each product individually. ... Planner Plan 1* | CFQ7TTC0HDB1 | Yes ... Project Plan 3* | CFQ7TTC0HDB0 | No

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: A self-service blocking policy change can take up to 72 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: It can take up to 72 hours for the policy to be disabled and changes to occur.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Changing the self-service policy does not affect existing trials or purchases.
claims.quote: Changing the value for AllowSelfServicePurchase or OnlyTrialsWithoutPaymentMethod only impacts trials or purchases made for the specified product from that point forward. Existing trials or purchases for the specified product aren't affected.

claims.where: Governance controls: OnlyTrialsWithoutPaymentMethod
claims.claim: OnlyTrialsWithoutPaymentMethod allows free trials without a payment method but prevents purchases.
claims.quote: Users can't make self-service purchases but can acquire free trials for products that don't require them to add a payment method. After the trial expires, a user can't buy the paid version of the product.

claims.where: Governance controls: licence requests when trials are disabled
claims.claim: Microsoft's Project page says users are offered a licence request instead when trials are disabled.
claims.quote: If trials are disabled, users won't be allowed to start a trial, but rather will be given the ability to request a license for Microsoft Project.

claims.where: controls[2].ui and controls[2].api; Governance controls: separate switch
claims.claim: A separate sprints-and-backlogs switch, distinct from the user's licence, is not documented on either the admin UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner unified plans sprints backlogs automatically enabled default administrator switch Set-PlannerConfiguration; Planner sprints backlogs unified plans Microsoft Graph beta plan sprint settings PowerShell. Read configuration excerpts and beta plan reference; no sprint-specific switch.

claims.where: Open questions: Planner unified plans Graph API
claims.claim: A Planner unified plans Graph API plan resource exists in beta.
claims.quote: Represents a plan in the Planner Unified plans Graph API. ... APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.where: rationale: cost
claims.claim: In premium plans, Microsoft 365 users have view-only access to premium capabilities not included in their licence.
claims.quote: In premium plans, Microsoft 365 users can use the capabilities included with their license and have view-only access to all other premium capabilities.

claims.where: front matter: cost; rationale: cost; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The known licence basis involves paid Planner Plan 1 or Planner and Project Plan 3 subscriptions for a subset of users, while unified-plan sprint entitlement remains unpublished.
claims.quote: Planner Plan 1: $10.00 user/month, paid yearly ... Backlogs and sprints; Planner and Project Plan 3: $30.00 user/month, paid yearly ... Everything in Planner Plan 1
